title: Token ID offset regression during batched weight swap
content:
Summary:

Short: During a staged batched-weight swap for model version 2.3.0 -> 2.3.1 we observed a token-ID offset regression impacting ~8% of routed traffic in region us-west1. Symptoms included garbled completions, systematic hallucinations anchored to off-by-N token mappings, and elevated user-error reports. The rollout was paused and a rollback performed. This doc captures timeline, root cause hypotheses, fixes applied, and runbook changes.

Impact: 
- Client-facing text-generation calls returned semantically incorrect responses for ~8% of traffic serviced by the new pool (estimated 4k requests/min at peak).
- Error rates (invalid-response classification) rose from baseline 0.3% to 5.7% on affected routes.
- No data exfiltration; correctness regression only.
- No SLOs violated for availability; latency mildly increased for affected nodes while retry logic fired.

Detection: 
- 2025-11-02 09:12 PST: Observability alert (metrics pipeline) flagged a sharp spike in rouge-token-rate for /v1/generate on model redwood/gpt-2.3.1-quantized.
- 09:14 PST: First customer support ticket describing "weird word substitutions" for a high-traffic customer.
- 09:18 PST: SRE oncall started triage after correlating the spikes with deployments to dedicated pool rdw-prd-usw1.

Initial containment actions taken: 
- 09:26 PST: Paused staged weight swap pipeline (blocked further nodes from switching).
- 09:31 PST: Disabled smart-routing to new pool and routed traffic to stable v2.3.0 pool via routing policy override.
- 09:42 PST: Forced cache-drain on nodes that had already swapped weights to attempt tokeniser reset (no material improvement).
- 10:05 PST: Decided to roll back model instances that had completed weight swap to previous image artifact and perform full restart sequence.

Timeline (condensed):
- 08:55 PST: Orchestrator job triggered batched-weight-swap job 2025-11-02-08:55 (staged by routing-based health checks).
- 09:10 PST: First health probe mis-match in pool A (small L7 503 flake). Automated retry allowed more nodes to progress.
- 09:12 PST: Metrics spike; alert triggers.
- 09:26 PST: Pipeline paused.
- 09:40 PST: Initial hypothesis surfaced about tokenizer mismatch caused by config templating.
- 10:30 PST: Rollback completed for first tranche; metric trends began improving by 10:50 PST.
- 13:00 PST: Full rollback and verification declared complete. Post-incident monitoring window declared 72 hours.

Diagnostic evidence: 
- Saved sample payloads show consistent token ID shift: input token IDs mapped to vocabulary index +5 relative to expected tokenizer map for affected responses.
- Node-level logs show tokenizer checksum mismatch warnings during startup on ~12% of nodes in pool A. These warnings were logged at INFO and did not trip fail-fast.
- Deployment job logs: templating step used environment variable TOKENIZER_MAP_PATH that resolves differently depending on base image (alpine vs debian), leading to a stale symlink being written when a particular bootstrap path exists.
- KV-cache metrics: prefix cache miss rate remained normal, but per-shard kv-cache-validity flags were inconsistent after in-place weight apply.

Root cause (summary): 
A combination of two issues allowed a tokenizer-vocab mismatch to reach production during a batched weight swap: 
1) Config templating bug in the rollout job: when bootstrapping certain worker images the deployment script wrote a symlink to /app/tokenizer/current that pointed to a previous vocab shard (artifact v2.2), not the new v2.3 tokenizer. The templating logic lacks an explicit atomic replace and falls back to a write-if-missing path.
2) The weight-swap process is a zero-downtime in-place apply that expects tokenizer invariants to be satisfiable across versions. In this case some nodes applied weights first and served requests before their tokenizer symlink refresh completed. Because tokenizer checks were only advisory (INFO logs) the serving runtime did not refuse to serve mismatched weights.

Contributing factors: 
- Rollout pipeline assumed tokenizer mapping is stable across minor releases; there was no explicit tokenizer-version preflight test in the health check.
- Observability for tokenizer-vocab mismatches is coarse: checksum warnings were at INFO and not surfaced as alerts.
- The canary size and selection policy allowed the affected subset to constitute a non-trivial portion of traffic (~8%) before pause.

Why this escaped earlier detection: 
- Integration test suites exercised model correctness in unit tests but not the combined weight-swap + tokenizer symlink path used in the staged rollout.
- The templating bug only triggers on images with older filesystem layout (present in ~15% of fleet); test infra does not spin up that exact base image.

Mitigation and rollback details: 
- Immediate: paused rollout, routed traffic away, rolled back swapped nodes to known-good artifact, restarted nodes with explicit tokenizer refresh.
- Near-term hotfix: updated rollout job script (PR #7890) to perform atomic symlink replace and to verify tokenizer checksum post-bootstrap. Added a fail-fast check to block node from entering ready state if checksum mismatches. Deployed to staging and then prod.
- Observability: updated metrics to emit tokenizer_checksum_mismatch as an error-level gauge and added an alert when mismatch_rate > 0.1% over 60s.

Permanent corrective actions (action items): 
1) Add preflight token mapping test to rollout health checks that performs round-trip token->text->token for a set of deterministic inputs. Owner: Marcus Liang. ETA: 2026-01-15.
2) Change batch weight-swap to include a tokenizer-compatibility gate: node must pass tokenizer checksum verification before accepting traffic. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. ETA: 2026-01-05.
3) Harden templating library: forbid write-if-missing for symlinks used by runtime; always perform atomic replace. Owner: Release Engineering (Renata Souza). ETA: 2025-12-08.
4) Add integration test that uses the legacy base image layout used by ~15% of fleet to catch the symlink path. Owner: CI Team. ETA: 2025-12-01.
5) Run a one-off sweep of fleet to surface any remaining nodes with mixed tokenizer artifacts and force-refresh them. Owner: SRE Ops. ETA: 2025-11-10 (completed).
6) Update runbook: new step "verify-tokenizer-checksum" added to model-deploy-runbook and a troubleshooting checklist for token-id offset. Owner: Asha Patel. ETA: 2025-11-15.

Runbook / Playbook changes required: 
- Add explicit check in "preflight checks" for tokenizer checksum equality between artifact and node.
- Promote tokenizer mismatch logs to error severity.
- Update rollback instructions to include forced tokenizer cache invalidation and a verification command snippet: curl --header 'x-test-tokenize: true' https://internal-tokenizer-check/redwood/gpt-2.3.1 | jq .tokens
- Add a simple fuzz test to the canary verifier that asserts token id parity for a small corpus.

Postmortem follow-up actions and verification: 
- Post-deploy verification window established for 72 hours; run queries in regression harness (Priya).
- CI integration tests updated and merged (PR #7905).
- Release engineering executed a fleet sweep and reported 0 remaining legacy-symlink nodes after 2025-11-10.

Open questions / To investigate further: 
- How many other rollout jobs use similar write-if-missing symlink pattern? (we suspect 3 templates).
- Should tokenizer version pinning be mandatory for minor releases, not optional? pros/cons listed in the doc body.
- Explore whether KV cache invalidation race contributed to observed garbling even after symlink corrected. Add dedicated test.

Appendix: artifacts and snippets:
- Example mismatch log: 
  2025-11-02T09:11:03Z INFO tokenizer: checksum expected=0x4f3a2c found=0x1e7b9d path=/app/tokenizer/current (will continue)
- Suggested verification command (internal): 
  docker run --rm redwood/runtime:v2.3.1 /bin/bash -c "python -c 'from tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer("default"); print(t.encode("hello world"))'"

Post-incident notes (informal): 
- Observability saved us here; the rouge-token metric was the early-warning signal. Shoutout to the metrics team for the quick dashboard edit.
- We need a stricter definition of "ready-to-serve" for zero-downtime applies; tokenization invariants should be first-class.
- This doc is a working draft; please add comments and link additional artifacts.

Owners and reviewers: 
- Incident owner: Asha Patel (SRE)
- Primary eng owner for fixes: Renata Souza (Release Eng)
- Serving runtime: Marcus Liang
- QA / Regression harness: Priya Menon

Status: in_review — aiming to finalize and ship runbook updates and PRs by 2026-01-15.
